# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 12 (LOGOS Formal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 12
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Similarly, concerning the cross, he speaks again in Moses — when Israel was being attacked by foreigners — in order to remind those who were under attack that they had been handed over to death on account of their sins. The Spirit speaks to the heart of Moses to make a type of the cross and of him who was to suffer, because, as he says, unless they set their hope in him, war shall prevail over them forever.
2. Moses therefore placed one weapon upon another in the midst of the fight; and standing higher than all of them, he stretched out his hands; and in this way Israel again prevailed. But then whenever he let down his hands, they began to be slain.
3. Why? So that they might know that they are unable to be saved unless they set their hope in him.
4. And again in another prophet he says: "All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient people who contradicted my righteous way."
5. And again Moses makes a type of Jesus — showing that he must suffer and himself give life, though they would believe they had destroyed him — by the sign given when Israel fell by the serpent: for the Lord placed a serpent on a pole, saying: "Shall everyone who is bitten by the serpent, looking upon it, be saved?" — since in a serpent there is no salvation at all.
6. And again he has glory in the midst of these types. For the Father says to the Son: "Let us make the human being according to our image and likeness, and let them have dominion over the beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven and the fish of the sea." And when the Lord saw his beautiful creation he said: "Increase and multiply and fill the earth." These things were spoken to the Son.
7. I will also show you how the Lord speaks to us. He made a second creation in the last days. The Lord says: "Behold, I make the last things as the first." For this reason the prophet proclaimed to those who had perished in the sea, and to those in the deep, and to those dwelling in the chambers of death.
8. And further he says: "And there came forth from the mountains of Israel a shoot, and it grew and became great." The shoot is David, and the mountains of Israel are Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
9. And again: "In the last days the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, and the house of God shall be exalted above all the hills." This is the manifestation of our Lord.
